title: Set air movers to dry a wet room: outlets at the walls, 15-45 degrees, one way round
instruction: The carpet in this room is wet (1:16 scale; the wall nearest you is left out). Set the four air movers to dry it the way restoration crews do: two along each side wall, each with its black outlet no more than 15 mm (24 cm) from the wall and blowing into the wall at 15 to 45 degrees so the air sweeps along it, the two on each wall 190 to 305 mm (10 to 16 ft) apart, and all four blowing the same way round the room.
context: Water-damage restoration technicians and building maintenance staff dry flooded rooms with air movers, small snail-shell blowers. Restoration training based on the IICRC S500 standard for water damage restoration places them along the wet walls with the outlet at the base of the wall, aimed 15 to 45 degrees into it so the air sweeps along the wall and the carpet edge ('wall washing'), about one for every 10 to 16 ft of wet wall, and all blowing the same way round the room so the air turns as one vortex. Movers blowing straight at a wall, parallel to it or against each other leave slow-drying spots where mould can start. Setting them out is the first job after the water is extracted. Here a 1:16 room has two 18 ft side walls, so each takes two movers (the back wall's are left out to keep it to four).
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. A 1:16 room stands on the table. Its fourth wall, nearest the arms, is left out, and the other three are cut down to their bottom 10 mm (16 cm) so the camera sees the floor. Fixed: (1) Wet carpet: a mid-grey felt sheet 1 mm thick, x 12.0 to 47.0 cm, y -18.5 to +18.5 cm (5.6 x 5.9 m). (2) Left wall: off-white painted MDF, 10 mm thick and 10 mm tall, x 12.0 to 48.0 cm, y +18.5 to +19.5 cm, standing on the table along the carpet's left edge; its face (the room side) is at y +18.5 cm. (3) Right wall: the same, x 12.0 to 48.0 cm, y -19.5 to -18.5 cm; its face is at y -18.5 cm. (4) Back wall: the same, x 47.0 to 48.0 cm, y -18.5 to +18.5 cm. Loose: (5) Four air movers, each one rigid 25 g body: a blue plastic housing 30 mm long (along the airflow), 26 mm wide and 30 mm tall, painted black over its front 5 mm (the outlet end) so the top view shows which way it blows; a black plastic outlet 5 mm deep, 26 mm wide and 12 mm tall across the bottom of its front face, where the air comes out; and a grey plastic handle 20 x 10 x 6 mm on top, along the airflow. The whole mover is 35 mm long and 36 mm tall. A mover's centre is the middle of the housing's base, 15 mm behind the housing's front face. All four stand upright on the carpet blowing toward the right wall (outlets toward -y): air mover 1 centred at x 33.0 cm, y +13.0 cm; air mover 2 at x 42.0 cm, y +13.0 cm; air mover 3 at x 33.0 cm, y -13.0 cm; air mover 4 at x 42.0 cm, y -13.0 cm. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: The score is read from the four movers' poses at the last step, as a top photo with a tape and a protractor would read it. A mover's airflow is the direction from the back of its housing to its outlet, seen from above. Placed: tilted 10 degrees or less, its lowest point within 3 mm of the carpet, its centre inside the room (over the carpet), and still (moved under 5 mm over the last 0.5 s, turns counted at its corners). It blows into the left wall (face at y +18.5 cm) if its airflow points to +y at all, into the right wall (face at y -18.5 cm) if to -y. Its angle into that wall is the angle between the airflow and the wall seen from above (0 along the wall, 90 straight at it); its gap is the distance, square to the wall, from the outlet's nearest point to the line of that wall's face (touching is 0). A mover is set when it is placed, its angle into the wall is 15 to 45 degrees and its gap is 15 mm or less. It goes clockwise round the room, seen from above, if its airflow points away from the arms (+x) along the left wall or toward them (-x) along the right wall; anticlockwise the reverse. For each way round, each side wall credits the movers set on it going that way: none 0, one 1, two or more 2 if some two of them have centres 190 to 305 mm (10 to 16 ft) apart along the wall (in x), else 1; so a wall credits at most two. The score is 0.25 times the larger of the two ways' totals (left wall plus right wall): 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 or 1.0. Either way round can score 1.0, and the trial ends early once 1.0 has held for 3 s. Score 0 if no mover is set. Examples: the start (all four blowing straight at the right wall) 0; all four set the same way round, two per wall 230 mm apart, 1.0; three right and the fourth at 60 degrees into its wall, or with its outlet 20 mm off the wall, 0.75; one wall's pair right and the other wall's two set 100 mm apart, 0.75; both walls' pairs set but all blowing toward the back wall (two parallel streams, no loop) 0.5; one clockwise and one anticlockwise on each wall 0.5; one wall's pair right, the other two left in the middle, 0.5; one mover set 0.25; all four under 15 degrees to their walls, pointed straight at them, blowing away from them, lifted or on their sides 0. In a real trial: a protractor against the wall's face on a top photo for the angle, a ruler from the wall to the outlet's corner for the gap, a tape between the housings' centres along the wall for the spacing.
fidelity: A 1:16 model with the simulator's default friction. The carpet and walls are fixed; each air mover is one 25 g rigid body of coloured boxes (housing, outlet, handle) with no fan, cord or wheels. No airflow or drying is simulated: the task scores the set-up restoration training teaches, which a tape and a protractor check. The walls are cut down to 16 cm so the camera sees the floor. The scorer sees only the movers, so one held still within 3 mm of the carpet counts as placed.
reset_notes: Stand the four air movers upright on the carpet, all blowing toward the right wall (outlets toward -y): air mover 1 centred at x 33.0 cm, y +13.0 cm; air mover 2 at x 42.0 cm, y +13.0 cm; air mover 3 at x 33.0 cm, y -13.0 cm; air mover 4 at x 42.0 cm, y -13.0 cm (a mover's centre is the middle of its housing's base). The carpet and walls are fixed. Nothing is consumed.
